messages:
anya: saw a flaky in staging where two nodes thought they owned prefix/tenantZ/bar after a fast handoff. served stale reads for ~20s.

derek: can you paste the minimal log?

anya: snippet:
```
[2026-02-12T09:07:12Z] node-12: mark resident tenantZ/bar slot=5
[2026-02-12T09:07:13Z] node-3: mark resident tenantZ/bar slot=9
[2026-02-12T09:07:30Z] read -> stale value from node-12
```

priya: similar to earlier threads. two options we keep debating: epoch CAS (atomic counter) vs reservation cookie (nonce).

kevin: quick pros: epoch CAS = simple correctness invariant, easier to reason about and proofs. cookie = lightweight, fewer metadata bumps but more RPC logic and TTL tuning.

anya: ops concern: Dedicated/Private metadata stores have higher variance; cookies with tight TTLs may misfire there.

derek: what about a hybrid: reader-side lightweight validation + epoch CAS for claim path in hosted? readers reject obvious mismatches and scars are caught by epoch for claims.

kevin: hybrid seems pragmatic. propose:
1) add reader validation on cache hit/miss that checks owner_id + seen_epoch and increments reader.stale_hit_rejects metric
2) implement epoch CAS for claim RPC in hosted with optional metadata field epoch (default 0)
3) feature-flag reservation cookie for aggressive handoff cases only

priya: test plan: deterministic sim for demote/claim/retry interleavings + chaos job that drops demote acks. metrics: double_residency, reader.stale_hit_rejects, claim.epoch_bumps.

ops-bot: created metric tiles: evict.double_residency, reader.stale_hit_rejects (user=ops-bot, id=EVICT-601)

anya: rollout: reader validation everywhere first (emit only), then epoch CAS on 20% hosted shards, run 6h chaos, if green expand. keep Private on reader-only until control plane SD is upgraded.

kevin: I'll own PR for epoch CAS + unit sim. priya will own chaos. I'll add trace tags for epoch and claim_result.

priya: adding note to GH#5250 with repro and sim harness. will attach logs after first canary.

anya: thanks all. last_message: kicking off the reader-validation canary now.
